notes:
Summary:
- Product: TestPilot Agents builds an IDE-integrated code agent platform (in-editor copilots + CI agents). Seeking low-latency streaming for in-IDE completions and deterministic behavior for CI flows.
- Primary ask: function/tool calling for code agent workflows: remote test runner, linter invocation, build-log retrieval, binary launches inside a sandboxed executor, artifact capture, and ephemeral credential handling.
Business context and constraints:
- Mid-market vendor with 120 engineers; several regulated customers require on-prem or VPC deployments. Some teams run in air-gapped data centers for regulated customers.
- Cost sensitivity on hosted inference; will consider Dedicated for predictable throughput for CI agents.
Technical requirements (from calls):
- Tool/function calling primitives: agent->run_test(command, env, timeout) -> returns verdict + artifacts link; agent->run_lint(files) -> structured diagnostics; agent->stream_build_logs(build_id) -> incremental stdout/stderr. Need stable JSON schemas for responses.
- Sandboxing: container- or microVM-based execution with CPU/memory constraints, chroot/namespace isolation, network egress controls, and strict artifact retention TTLs. Must support ephemeral credentials for accessing internal package registries.
- Streaming: WebSocket/HTTP2 streaming to editor with tokenized partial outputs, pty-friendly streaming for test runners, and ability to pause/seek logs. Typical latency targets: 50-150ms for token streaming in-editor; CI agents can accept 200-400ms.
- Model/version pinning: deterministic pinning for CI (so test-related suggestions and fixes are reproducible across runs). Want tooling to pin model+quant config at repo or pipeline level.
- Fallbacks & routing: ability to route editor traffic to low-latency hosted replicas, and route CI-heavy workloads to Dedicated/private clusters to control cost.
- Observability: per-request trace ids, tie artifacts to traces, and retention policy for logs (90d default, configurable).
